Alex R: starting night handoff — taking over primary for 00:00-08:00 PST. quick summary of the last 12h and outstanding items.
incident-bot: INCIDENT 3247 | 2026-11-03 19:42 UTC | pages: alex.r, priya.s | severity: P2 | summary: downstream KV cache thrash causing elevated latency and 429s on hosted-api. automatic fallback triggered to cheaper-variant model.
Priya S: yep. root cause appears to be a regression in the batcher memory accounting after the recent optimization. we saw continuous batch sizes spike from ~8->120 for some long-seq requests, which pushed a couple of GPU pools into OOM soft-fallover and triggered our throttle.
Mateo G: mitigation applied at 20:05 UTC — reverted the batch-size estimator change in the canary, forced new deploy to dedicated pool, and disabled continuous-batching for the problematic route. KPIs improved within ~3 minutes.
Jordan L: customer impact: small set of high-QPS tenants experienced 429s for ~11m, most traffic gracefully fell back to canonical-model with slightly higher cost. no data loss. we opened tickets with affected customers: CS case #5679, #5680. notified account teams.
Sam T: monitoring: alert fatigue note — paging thresholds were too tight for that route. I lowered page threshold from 5% errors in 2m -> 10% in 5m for hosted-api-route-X to reduce noisy pagering. created follow-up task to tune SLO-derived thresholds.
Priya S: outstanding items to watch tonight:
- revert validation: confirm no other routes are running the bad estimator (grep + canary logs). command I used:
```
# list canary deploys with custom batcher
rg "batcher_estimator" -n /var/log/deploys | awk -F: '{print $1}' | sort -u
```
- keep an eye on pool mem pressure metrics: gpu_mem_alloc_pct and batcher_heap_usage.
- ensure KV cache hit-rate stays >= 92% for low-latency tier.
Alex R: coverage / who is where — primary/secondary assignments for the shift:
- primary: Alex R (pager)
- secondary: Priya S (escalation & infra)
- backup: Mateo G (pool ops)
- shadow: Jordan L (customer comms)
rotation-bot: Reminder: on-call rotation change scheduled at 02:00 PST — Alex R will hand to Jordan L as primary if no critical pages escalate before then.
Jordan L: noted. I'll be primary 02:00-10:00 PST if everything stays quiet.
Priya S: runbook pointers for tonight (shortcuts):
- KV/cache thrash: runbook link https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-thrash (steps 1-6, rollback snippets)
- Batcher OOM/fallback: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/batcher-oom (section 3: disable continuous-batching)
- Model fallback: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-fallback (how to pin to canonical-variant)
Sam T: quick checklist I left in the incident thread:
- confirm canary rollback completed (done)
- validate autoscaler cooldowns (set to 120s temporarily)
- confirm fallback model latency delta < 50ms for major tenants
Alex R: next steps for the night (action items):
1) Priya to run a full grep across deploys for estimator flags and report by 01:00 PST. (Priya acknowledged)
2) Mateo to watch GPU pool mem and restart pool-7 if avg_alloc > 88% for 10m. (Mateo acked)
3) Jordan to keep CS loop posted and escalate if >3 tenants with recurring 429s. (Jordan acked)
4) Sam to follow up on alert thresholds and open a small RFC to adjust SLO thresholds for route-X. (Sam acked)
Priya S: ACK. I'll paste the quick query I'll run in case it helps others to re-run:
```
# check for active estimator flag
kubectl -n prod get deploy -l app=batcher -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}: {.spec.template.spec.containers[*].env}' | rg "batcher_estimator"
```
Jordan L: customer comms template in case we need to update status page:
> We're mitigating elevated latency and transient errors affecting a subset of inference traffic. fallback routing is active; we continue to monitor and expect normal service within the hour. — support@redwood
Alex R: closing notes: no open P1s. service is in steady state but still fragile for long-seq workloads. prefer to be conservative with continuous-batching toggles until we have a longer canary. ping me in-thread for any new pages. good handoff, team :thumbsup:
incident-bot: RESOLVED 3247 | 2026-11-03 20:18 UTC | resolution: revert + disable continuous-batching for route-X. metrics back within SLOs.
